check_service_status.description: Check whether ColorMagic is answering, and how quickly, by running a small search. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can branch on it and fall back to a saved palette when the service is down. Being throttled is reported separately from being down. No API key required.

mock_response.message: ColorMagic is up and serving palettes: 20 matched 'blue'.

check_service_status.name: check_service_status

message.description: What happened, in a sentence worth posting.

online.description: True when the service answered with a list of palettes. This is the field to branch on.

palettes_found.description: How many palettes the probe search for blue matched, or null when the service did not answer with a list.

rate_limited.description: True when the answer was a throttle (HTTP 429). Being throttled is not the same as being down.

reachable.description: True when something answered at all, even with an error. False means the request never landed.

response_time_ms.description: How long the request took, in milliseconds, or null when nothing came back.

status_code.description: The HTTP status that came back, or null when nothing did.

find_palette.description: Get the one palette on ColorMagic that best fits a search: the most liked match by default, or the newest, or the first the service returns. The step for a workflow that wants a palette to use rather than a list to choose from. Keep only palettes carrying one tag. Fails when nothing matches, so a step downstream never posts an empty palette. No API key required.
find_palette.name: find_palette

parameters.description: A word or short phrase to search palettes for. ColorMagic matches it against palette names and tags, so a color (green), a mood (calm), a season (autumn), a style (retro, pastel, 70s) or a subject (ocean, wedding, coffee shop) all work.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Optional. Keep only the palettes that carry this tag, as it appears in a palette's tags: a color, a mood, a season or a style, such as pastel, warm, spring or vintage. Case does not matter. Use it to narrow a broad search, e.g. search for green and keep only pastel.
parameters.name: tag

parameters.description: Optional. Which of the matching palettes to return. Most liked is the one the most people liked; newest is the most recently generated; first is the top result in ColorMagic's own order. Most liked by default.
parameters.name: pick

palette.description: One palette: five colors with a name, tags and likes.

colors.description: The palette's five colors as hex codes with the # on, lower-case, in the order ColorMagic arranges them, e.g. #44562f.

colors_text.description: The same five colors as one comma-separated line, ready to post: #44562f, #83934d, #b7c88d, #e9dfb4, #efbfb3.

created_at.description: When the palette was generated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

likes.description: How many people have liked the palette on ColorMagic.

name.description: The palette's name, as ColorMagic generated it, e.g. Florest Moth.

normalized_hash.description: A fingerprint of the palette's colors, the same for two palettes made of the same colors, so a workflow can spot a duplicate it has already used.

tags.description: The tags the palette carries, lower-case: colors, moods, seasons and styles such as green, pastel, spring or retro. Any of them can be searched for or filtered on.

url.description: The palette's own page on ColorMagic, e.g. https://colormagic.app/palette/671fd5edab6cc866507fe7cf.

pick.description: How the palette was chosen: most_liked, newest or first.

query.description: The search that was run, as it was sent.

tag.description: The tag the palettes were required to carry, lower-case, or null when none was asked for.

total_matches.description: How many palettes ColorMagic matched to the search, before the tag filter and any limit.

get_random_palette.description: Get one palette chosen at random from those on ColorMagic matching a search. A different palette every run, so a palette of the day for a channel, a newsletter or a mood board does not repeat itself. Keep only palettes carrying one tag. Fails when nothing matches. No API key required.

search_palettes.description: Search the palettes people have generated on ColorMagic by a word or phrase: a color, a mood, a season, a style or a subject, such as ocean, pastel, 70s or wedding. Each palette comes back with its five hex codes, its name, its tags, its likes and a link to its page. Keep only palettes carrying one tag, sort them by relevance, likes or age, and choose how many to return. No API key required.

parameters.description: Optional. The order to return the palettes in. Relevance is ColorMagic's own order; most liked puts the palettes the most people liked first; newest puts the most recently generated first. Relevance by default.

parameters.description: Optional. At most how many palettes to return, between 1 and 100; 20 by default. ColorMagic decides how many a search matches; this only trims the list.

description: Search the color palettes people have generated on ColorMagic, the free AI color palette generator, by mood, theme, season, style or color: ocean, pastel, 70s, wedding. Every palette comes back as five hex codes ready for a design brief, a slide, a chart or a CSS variable, with its name, its tags, how many people liked it and a link to it on ColorMagic. Take the whole list, the most liked match, or one at random for a palette of the day. No account or API key required.
